sa.title: School sign-in
sa.intro: Let people sign in to Darsi with their school accounts: Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak or any OpenID Connect provider. Nobody becomes an admin this way: new people join as students, or as teachers by your rule.
sa.switchOff: School sign-in is switched off for the whole platform by Darsi’s team. You can set it up, but nobody can use it until it is switched on.
sa.keyOff: School sign-in isn’t available on Darsi yet: its keys aren’t set up. Ask Darsi’s team.
sa.saved: Saved. You can come back to this later.
sa.editing: You are editing the live connection. It keeps working as it is until your changes pass a test; then they replace it.
sa.p.title: Which service do your school accounts use?
sa.p.googleD: School accounts on Google, such as @school.edu addresses in Gmail.
sa.p.microsoftD: School accounts on Microsoft 365 (formerly Azure AD).
sa.p.oktaD: Your school signs people in with Okta.
sa.p.keycloakD: Your school runs its own Keycloak server.
sa.p.oidcD: Any service that supports OpenID Connect.
sa.c.title: Connect Darsi to {provider}
sa.c.redirectHint: Use exactly this address, never a wildcard.
sa.c.signinLinkHint: If the console asks for a home page or sign-in address, use this one.
sa.c.copyManual: Couldn’t copy. Select it and copy it yourself:
sa.c.fields: What Darsi needs from the console
sa.c.okNoPkce: It doesn’t say whether it supports PKCE. Darsi uses it anyway.
sa.c.okEnd: It has a sign-out page Darsi can link to.
sa.f.tenantHint: A GUID from the app’s Overview page. Not “common” or “organizations”.
sa.f.domainOkta: Your Okta domain, such as school.okta.com
sa.f.domainKc: Your Keycloak server, such as login.school.edu
sa.f.oktaServerHint: Only for a custom authorization server: “default” or its ID.
sa.f.realmHint: The realm your school’s accounts are in.
sa.f.issuerHint: Such as https://login.school.edu. Darsi reads everything else from it.
sa.f.secretMs: Client secret (its Value, not its Secret ID)
sa.f.secretHint: Saved encrypted at the end of the next step. Darsi never shows it again.
sa.f.secretSaved: A secret is saved. Type a new one only to replace it.
sa.f.secretExpiresHint: Darsi reminds you before it runs out.
sa.f.secretExpiresBad: Choose a date no more than three years from now, or leave it empty.
sa.f.openToAll: Everyone my provider signs in may join
sa.cs.google-client-web: In the Google Cloud console, open APIs & Services, then Credentials, and create an OAuth client ID of type “Web application”.
sa.cs.google-internal: On the OAuth consent screen, choose “Internal”, so only your Workspace’s accounts can use it.
sa.cs.google-cloud-access: In the Google Admin console, make sure the admin setting this up may use Google Cloud.
sa.cs.google-under18: If students are under 18, allow Darsi in Security, API controls, App access control, for their organizational units.
sa.cs.google-redirect: Under “Authorized redirect URIs”, add the redirect URI below.
sa.cs.google-copy-secret: Create the client, then copy its Client ID and Client secret into the fields below.
sa.cs.ms-register-single-tenant: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations, choose New registration, and pick “Accounts in this organizational directory only”.
sa.cs.ms-web-platform: Under Redirect URI, choose the platform “Web”.
sa.cs.ms-redirect: Enter the redirect URI below, then choose Register.
sa.cs.ms-secret-value: In Certificates & secrets, make a new client secret and copy its Value (not its Secret ID) into the field below.
sa.cs.ms-optional-email: In Token configuration, add the optional claim “email” to the ID token.
sa.cs.ms-app-roles: In App roles, create the roles Teacher and Student, then give them to people in Enterprise applications, Users and groups.
sa.cs.ms-admin-consent: In API permissions, choose “Grant admin consent” for your organization.
sa.cs.okta-oidc-web: In the Okta Admin Console, open Applications, choose Create App Integration, then “OIDC - OpenID Connect” and “Web Application”.
sa.cs.okta-redirect: Under Sign-in redirect URIs, add the redirect URI below.
sa.cs.okta-assign-groups: Under Assignments, give the app to the groups of students and teachers who may use Darsi.
sa.cs.okta-custom-server: If you use a custom authorization server, note its ID (or “default”) for the field below. Otherwise leave that field empty.
sa.cs.okta-groups-claim: To tell teachers apart, add a “groups” claim to the ID token (Sign On, OpenID Connect ID Token, Groups claim).
sa.cs.kc-realm: Open the realm your school’s accounts are in.
sa.cs.kc-client: Create a client with the OpenID Connect protocol.
sa.cs.kc-redirect: Add the redirect URI below to Valid redirect URIs.
sa.cs.kc-client-auth: Switch on Client authentication, then copy the secret from the Credentials tab.
sa.cs.kc-groups-mapper: To tell teachers apart, add a Group Membership mapper named “groups” to the client’s dedicated scope, added to the ID token.
sa.cs.oidc-register: In your provider, register a new web application: a confidential OpenID Connect client.
sa.cs.oidc-redirect: Add the redirect URI below as its redirect or callback address.
sa.cs.oidc-confidential: Use the authorization code flow with a client secret.
sa.cs.oidc-email-claims: Make sure the ID token carries email and email_verified (the email and profile scopes).
sa.h.name-not-found: Darsi couldn’t find that name. Check the spelling of the domain or address.
sa.h.certificate-chain: The server’s HTTPS certificate chain is incomplete. Ask whoever runs it to install the intermediate certificates.
sa.h.certificate-name: The server’s HTTPS certificate is for another name.
sa.h.certificate: The server’s HTTPS certificate isn’t valid.
sa.h.unreachable: Darsi’s servers (Google Cloud, Belgium) couldn’t connect. Check that it can be reached from the internet, not only inside the school.
sa.h.timeout: It didn’t answer Darsi’s servers (Google Cloud, Belgium) in time. Check that it can be reached from the internet.
sa.h.blocked: That address is inside a private network, which Darsi never calls.
sa.h.redirect: It answered with a redirect. Give the exact address, not one that forwards.
sa.h.too-large: It answered with too much data.
sa.h.address: That isn’t a valid https address.
sa.h.busy: Darsi is busy checking providers. Try again in a minute.
sa.h.bad-answer: It answered, but not with what Darsi expected.
sa.h.document: Its OpenID Connect discovery document is missing or isn’t valid.
sa.h.issuer-mismatch: The provider calls itself {got}, but Darsi expected {want}. Check the address you typed.
sa.h.endpoint: One of its addresses isn’t a valid https address.
sa.h.pkce: It doesn’t support PKCE with S256, which Darsi needs.
sa.h.alg: It doesn’t sign ID tokens with RS256, PS256 or ES256.
sa.h.response-type: It doesn’t support the authorization code flow.
sa.h.auth-method: It doesn’t accept a client secret in a way Darsi supports (Basic or POST).
sa.h.constants: Its addresses aren’t the ones Darsi expects for this provider.
sa.w.title: Who can sign in
sa.w.domainsHint: One or more, separated by commas, such as school.edu, students.school.edu. Personal mail domains like gmail.com aren’t allowed.
sa.w.domainsGoogle: Required for Google: only accounts in these domains can sign in.
sa.w.openToAllD: No domain check. Choose this only if your provider has school accounts and nothing else.
sa.w.needOne: Give at least one domain, or choose that everyone your provider signs in may join.
sa.w.verified: My provider’s email addresses are checked by the school
sa.w.verifiedD: Treat every address it sends as verified. Leave this off unless the school issues all of them.
sa.w.teacherOff: Everyone who joins this way is a student. You can change roles later, on People.
sa.w.tGoogleNeed: Give a domain or at least one address.
sa.w.tRoleD: People given this app role in Entra (Enterprise applications, Users and groups).
sa.w.tGroupD: Members of this security group. Entra sends group IDs: paste the group’s Object ID.
sa.w.tSeen: The last test saw these values:
sa.w.classHint: Optional: a claim holding the person’s class (short text, up to 40 characters). Used only when the account is made.
sa.w.sessionHint: From 1 to 90 days. People who sign in only through the school are signed out after this.
sa.w.personalD: Skip the account chooser. Leave this off if people share computers.
sa.m.title: {n} people are connected to this sign-in
sa.m.title.one: {n} person is connected to this sign-in
sa.m.body: You changed the provider or the app. Are they the same people?
sa.m.same: The same people: a new app registration at the same provider
sa.m.sameD: They keep their accounts and sign in as before.
sa.m.newD: Each person is matched again by their verified email at their next sign-in. Anyone not matched joins afresh.
sa.m.issuerChanged: The provider’s address changed, so this counts as a different provider.
sa.t.title: Test before anyone uses it
sa.t.intro: Sign in with your own school account to see what Darsi would do. Nothing is created or changed.
sa.t.studentD: Make a one-time link for a student account. It works once, for 24 hours. It creates nothing and signs nobody in.
sa.t.link: Send this link to a student:
sa.t.needSecret: Save the client secret first, on the Connect step.
sa.t.unsaved: You changed settings on an earlier step and haven't saved them. Save them first: the test uses what is saved.
sa.t.passed: The test passed for these settings.
sa.t.passedRefused: The connection works, but Darsi would refuse the person who tested it. See why below, then change the settings or test with another account.
sa.t.old: This result is for earlier settings. Test again.
sa.t.studentNeeded: For Google and Microsoft, also test with a student account, or confirm that you did:
sa.t.studentChecked: I checked sign-in with a student account
sa.r.title: Last test
sa.r.unverified: The provider didn’t say this address is verified.
sa.r.teacherNo: Teacher rule: not matched, so a student.
sa.d.signin: sign them in to their existing account.
sa.d.signin-raise: sign them in to their existing account and make them a teacher.
sa.d.link-org-made: connect them to the account your organization made for them.
sa.d.create-student: create a new student account for them.
sa.d.create-teacher: create a new teacher account for them.
sa.d.wait: wait: another first sign-in for this person was running. Try again.
sa.cl.preferred_username: Microsoft’s sign-in name, for the domain check
sa.cl.name: the name on a new account
sa.cl.oid: who the person is at Microsoft
sa.cl.xms_edov: Microsoft’s word that the address is verified
sa.o.title: Turn on school sign-in
sa.o.noTeachers: None: everyone joins as a student
sa.o.match: {n} accounts your organization made will be matched at their first school sign-in. Everyone else who already has an account connects it from Me.
sa.o.match.one: {n} account your organization made will be matched at its first school sign-in. Everyone else who already has an account connects it from Me.
sa.o.matchNone: People who already have a Darsi account connect it from Me. Everyone else gets a new account at their first school sign-in.
sa.rf.sso-last-way-in: At least one admin of your organization must be able to sign in with a password or Google, so nobody is locked out if the school’s sign-in stops working. Give an admin their own login first, then try again.
sa.rf.sso-untested: The settings changed since the last test that passed. Test again first.
sa.rf.sso-secret: The client secret is missing. Type it on the Connect step and save.
sa.rf.sso-student-test: Test with a student account first, or tick that you checked with one.
sa.rf.sso-key: School sign-in’s keys aren’t working on Darsi. Ask Darsi’s team.
sa.rf.sso-signer: Darsi can’t sign people in this way yet. Ask Darsi’s team.
sa.rf.sso-org-inactive: This organization isn’t active, so school sign-in can’t be used.
sa.rf.sso-issuer: Darsi doesn’t accept this provider: anyone can make an account there, or the tenant is a shared one.
sa.rf.sso-slug: Darsi couldn’t reserve the sign-in link. Try again in a moment.
sa.rf.sso-update: Darsi was updated. Reload the page and try again.
sa.rf.sso-recent: For your safety, sign in to Darsi again, then test once more.
sa.rf.sso-other-org: Only this organization’s admins (or Darsi’s team) can test it.
sa.rf.sso-login: This person signs in only through the school: add an email login first.
sa.rf.not-org-admin: Only this organization’s admins can do that.
sa.rf.not-super: Only Darsi’s platform admins can do that.
sa.rf.no-account: This person has no school sign-in here.
sa.s.onDHost: People can sign in with their school accounts at {host}.
sa.s.offD: School sign-in is off. Nobody can sign in this way until it is on again.
sa.s.expiresSoon: The client secret expires on {date}. Make a new one soon and save it with Edit.
sa.s.shareHint: People open it to sign in with their school. On your own web address the button shows on the sign-in page by itself.
sa.s.offBody: {n} people sign in only through the school: they can’t sign in until it is on again. People with their own login aren’t affected. Nothing is deleted.
sa.s.offBody.one: {n} person signs in only through the school: they can’t sign in until it is on again. People with their own login aren’t affected. Nothing is deleted.
sa.s.editNext: Continue the edit waiting for its test
sa.s.promoted: Your changes passed the test and are live now.
sa.pb.secret-mismatch: The saved client secret no longer fits the provider’s settings. Type it again (Edit, then Connect).
sa.pb.secret-key: Darsi couldn’t read the saved secret. Ask Darsi’s team.
sa.pb.secret-expiring: Days left before the client secret runs out: {hint}. Make a new one and save it (Edit, then Connect).
sa.pb.endpoints-moved: The provider’s addresses changed ({hint}). Test again before people are affected.
sa.pb.full: The organization reached the number of members school sign-in may make. Ask Darsi’s team.
sa.pb.token: The provider refused Darsi’s request ({hint}). Check the client ID and secret.
sa.pb.id-token: Darsi refused a sign-in answer from the provider ({hint}).
sa.l.title: School finder
sa.l.none: Ask to be listed so people can find your school by name on darsiai.org.
sa.l.requested: Waiting for Darsi’s team to list {name}.
sa.l.asked: Sent. Darsi’s team will look at it.
sa.x.title: For Darsi’s team
sa.x.ceiling: Most members school sign-in may make
sa.x.ceilingBad: A whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, or empty.
sa.ls.title: Listing requests ({n})
sa.ls.intro: Schools that asked to appear in the school finder on darsiai.org. Check the name, logo and where people continue before you approve.
sa.ls.none: No school is waiting to be listed.
sa.ls.name: Name shown
sa.sw.title: School sign-in for everyone
sa.sw.on: On: organizations can let people sign in with their school accounts.
sa.sw.off: Off: every school sign-in button is hidden and no school sign-in can start.
sa.sw.offAsk: Turn school sign-in off for everyone?
sa.sw.offBody: Nobody can sign in through a school until it is on again: people who sign in only that way are locked out meanwhile. Every school’s settings are kept.
